title: External dataset licence register
description: R8.1 (decision-quality-proof task 7.1). One entry per external dataset, carrying the six fields R8.1 names. THE CENTRAL DESIGN DECISION: every one of the six keys is REQUIRED to be PRESENT, and each is typed ['string','null']. A key may therefore be null - meaning 'not yet read from the licence text' - but it may never be OMITTED. That asymmetry is deliberate and is what makes R8.1's 'an absent field is named rather than defaulted' mechanical: a reader cannot silently drop a term, and a null is a positive assertion of ignorance rather than an absence that a permissive default could fill. `scripts/audit/dataset_licence_truth.py` reports any null field as `unavailable` -> SKIP, naming the field. A SKIP is not a PASS (I-7).

schema_version.description: Pinned. A reader that does not recognise the version reports unavailable rather than guessing at the shape.

datasets.description: One entry per external dataset. Emptiness is deliberately NOT constrained here (no `minItems`): an empty register means nobody wrote a wrong term, there are simply no terms, which is the canonical `unavailable` shape rather than a document defect. `dataset_licence_truth` owns it as the `declaration-empty` rule -> SKIP. Constraining it here would make 'nothing is declared' a FAIL, which misreports an absence as a defect.

datasetLicence.description: ONE OWNER FOR COMPLETENESS. The six R8.1 fields are deliberately NOT in `required`. If the schema required them, a dropped key would surface as `schema-invalid` -> FAIL, and a null key as `field-absent` -> SKIP - two verdicts for one fact, decided by which of two mechanisms noticed first. Completeness is therefore owned entirely by `dataset_licence_truth`, which treats an ABSENT key and a NULL key identically: both are 'nobody established this term' -> unavailable, named. What the schema owns is the complementary half: a term that is PRESENT must be well-formed, so `read_date` must parse as a date and a string term must be non-empty. Present-and-wrong is somebody's defect in this tree -> FAIL. Absent-or-null is an unread term -> SKIP.

dataset_id.description: R8.1 dataset identity. Null means not yet established.

licence_id.description: R8.1 licence identifier, as the licence text itself names it (e.g. an SPDX identifier, or the competition-rules clause reference when no SPDX identifier applies). NEVER a plausible guess: an invented identifier is worse than a null, because a null surfaces and a guess does not.

licence_text_uri.description: R8.1 licence-text URI. The location a human can read the terms at, not a landing page that merely mentions them.

read_date.description: R8.1 read date - when a human actually read the terms at that URI. Null while nobody has. This field is the reason the artifact cannot be filled in by an agent: reading requires accepting terms, which is an operator act.

permitted_use.description: R8.1 permitted use, stated in the licence's own scope terms. Null means unread, NOT 'any use'.

dataset_revision.description: R8.1 dataset revision. Pins which bytes the licence was read against, so a re-published dataset does not inherit a stale confirmation.

redistribution.description: The redistribution disposition task 7.1 names. `unknown` and null are distinct: `unknown` asserts that the terms were read and are genuinely silent or ambiguous; null asserts that they were not read. Neither is `permitted`.

notes.description: Free-form provenance notes. Never load-bearing for the verdict.

confirmation.description: Who established the terms, and - while nobody has - exactly what an operator must do. Recording the procedure in the artifact is what stops a null field becoming a mystery rather than a task.

confirmed.description: True only when every one of the six R8.1 fields is non-null AND a human recorded that they read the terms. The gate does not trust this flag on its own: it re-derives field completeness and FAILs on a `confirmed: true` entry that still carries a null field, because a flag that can disagree with its own subject is a claim, not evidence.

confirmed_by.description: The operator who read the terms. Null while unconfirmed.

procedure.description: The steps an operator must take to confirm. Required even when confirmed, so the record states how the confirmation was obtained.

blocked_on.description: Why this cannot be confirmed mechanically - e.g. terms behind an acceptance gate that an agent must not accept on an operator's behalf.
